_doc: Revert-verify mutants for req a00031b2-43cd-47fa-8486-4493e22f4386 (issue #4528) — `PropertyCleanupService.removeEmptyPropertiesFromContent` must not hand a data-bearing string to String.replace. ⛔ One mutant PER `.replace` site, as the issue mandates: M1 is the fixed site (the frontmatter block rewrite), M2 is the other site in the same method (the list-item prefix strip, whose replacement is a constant and therefore NOT data-bearing — the mutant proves the axes notice if it starts behaving otherwise). M3 is the control on the repair logic itself, so the byte-identity axes cannot pass by the repair having become a no-op. The axes live in packages/cli because the product path to this service (createCleanPropertiesService → apply clean-properties) is in packages/services, which no workflow jest-runs; packages/cli/jest.config.js maps BOTH @kitelev/exocortex-core and @kitelev/exocortex-services to package SOURCE, so the mutation is seen. Set `tree`/`subject` to YOUR checkout before running.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/services/PropertyCleanupService.ts

M1_string_replacement_restored._note: THE defect, restored verbatim: the replacement goes back to being a STRING built from the file's own frontmatter, so JS reads `$&`, `$`-backtick, `$'`, `$$` and `$1`..`$99` inside a surviving value as replacement patterns. Reddens every byte-identity axis (P1-P5) and the structural one; the controls that carry no `$` (P6 repair completeness, P7 populated list, P8 untouched asset) stay GREEN — which is what makes P1-P5 non-vacuous rather than a side effect of the repair breaking.

M2_list_item_strip_keeps_prefix._note: The OTHER `.replace` site of the same method (`item.replace(/^\s+- /, "")`), mandated by the issue as its own mutant. Its replacement is a CONSTANT, so it is not part of the $-class — but it decides whether a list item counts as empty. Substituting `"$&"` keeps the `- ` prefix, so an all-empty list stops looking empty and survives the repair: P6 (every empty form removed) reddens, while the populated-list control P7 stays green. ⛤ Its red set {P6} is a LITERAL SUBSET of M3's {P1,P2,P3,P6,P7}, and that is legitimate rather than redundancy: the two mutants edit DIFFERENT lines (the list-item strip at the `.replace` site vs the empty-value branch), the issue mandates one mutant per `.replace` site, and P6 is honestly sensitive to BOTH independent defects — a list that stops looking empty, and a repair that stops removing. Read the subset as "P6 has two owners", not as "M2 adds nothing" (integration-test-revert-verify §A110: a shared red set does not by itself prove two conjuncts are locked — here the proof is that M3 reddens four axes M2 cannot touch).

M3_repair_disabled._note: Control on the repair itself: stop removing empty scalar properties. Reddens every axis that asserts the empty key is GONE (P1, P2, P3, P6, P7) and leaves the pure byte-identity ones (P4, P5) and the no-op asset (P8) green. Without this mutant, P1/P3 could be satisfied by a repair that silently stopped working.

M4_assembly_adds_blank_line._note: Exists because folding the first three mutants into sets left P8 — the control saying an asset with nothing empty comes out byte-identical — reddened by NOTHING (integration-test-revert-verify §A130: the axis exists, the mutant for it does not; an unproven control manufactures confidence). Appending one newline to the assembled frontmatter keeps every LINE present, so the containment axes P1/P3/P4 and the regexp controls P6/P7 stay green, and only the byte-identity axis notices.
